body.target_estimand: \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)=\{T_\pi:\pi\in\Pi_G(\mathcal O_G)\}\), with numerical duplicates removed

sampling_model.design: The identification kernel takes exact population covariances on an arbitrary fixed view graph \(G\). The inherited inference layer may use one sourcewise independent and identically distributed paired sample for each observed edge together with every view-marginal sample.
sampling_model.units: Within each covariance source, observations are independent and identically distributed from the corresponding marginal of one target law \(P\). Different sources need not be independent because units may be reused.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment variable; the causal target is the finite set of shared-order structural coefficient tuples.
sampling_model.overlap: Only edges of \(G\) require paired measurements. The maintained class assumes one target population, centered finite-second-moment disturbances with independent coordinates within each view, component-aligned cross-view second moments, and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances. The generating law need not be Gaussian; unrestricted cross-coordinate cross-view dependence, selection, transport, and arbitrary off-model covariance arrays are excluded.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The new theorem is population-computational. Sampling uncertainty is handled only by the parent covariance-region inversion over empirical edge and marginal covariance blocks; no new rate, limit law, or continuum-region enumerator is claimed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3 identify the shared causal partial order and view-specific coefficient matrices by recursively recovering roots and preserving the residual LiMVAM under the paper's Assumption 2 correlation-and-diversity condition; the paper permits non-Gaussian disturbances. The present specialization instead adds component-aligned cross-view moments and positive-definite coordinate covariance blocks, with Gaussianity used only for existential completion witnesses.
Theorem 7 states that every partial positive-definite matrix with a fixed sparsity graph has a positive-definite completion exactly when the graph is chordal.
Theorem 3 shows that IDGraphs partitions the DAGs represented by an MPDAG into subclasses with identified, pairwise distinct total-effect functionals.

Theorem 1 establishes AMO enumeration, Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration, Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs, and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization.

Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives a framework that enumerates equivalence classes represented by local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph with polynomial delay.
Theorem 7 gives an output-dependent delay bound after linear preprocessing for projected star-query enumeration by heavy-light partitioning and interleaving.
Reverse search enumerates a connected family from a locally computable parent map without retaining a global visited set.
Fraction-free Gaussian elimination uses exact divisibility from Sylvester's identity to prevent the exponential intermediate growth of naive fraction-producing elimination.

body.tldr: Many common orders can encode the same coefficient tuple in the component-aligned LiMVAM subclass with centered finite-second-moment, within-view independent disturbances, so traversing every compatible order can be factorial even when the causal output is a singleton. The generating law need not be Gaussian; component alignment and positive-definite coordinate disturbance covariances remain maintained restrictions, while Gaussian coordinate stacks are used only to construct existential completion witnesses. The population algorithm labels each removed-set transition by the immutable original-label regression row \(\beta(A,r)=\Sigma[r,A]\Sigma[A,A]^{-1}\), prunes dead subset states, interns exact rows, and merges equal live fragments. The central claims establish arbitrary-view-graph path exactness with positive-definite coordinate-noise completion, prove that live-fragment equality is exactly a right congruence for numerical completions, charge each fragment bucket to the final tuple set, and enumerate \(\Theta_G(\mathcal O_G)\) exactly once in \(O(\operatorname{poly}(p,m)2^p\max\{1,N_{\mathrm{out}}\})\) ordered exact-real time and space.

project_justification.gap: The parent calibration frontier has a \(2^p\)-state compatibility graph but no noncircular way to enumerate distinct numerical tuples without traversing all compatible paths. Published causal enumeration partitions graph classes by graphical effect formulas or lists graph-distinct DAGs, while general quotient enumeration assumes local decomposability not established for covariance-dependent coefficient equality.
project_justification.niche: At a fixed removed set \(A\), every future compatibility test depends only on the Schur residual state, and the row assigned when \(r\) is removed is the immutable original-label regression \(\beta(A,r)\). After source-to-sink pruning, the resulting fragments have nonempty, either identical or disjoint, completion sets.
project_justification.fill: Exact row interning and deterministic integer tries implement the fragment quotient without a real hash oracle. The projection lemma bounds every subset bucket by \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the maintained-model completion theorem certifies that each sink is a genuine arbitrary-pairing component-aligned mechanism. The generating law needs only centered finite second moments and within-view disturbance independence; Gaussian coordinate stacks are introduced solely to realize each positive-definite existential completion witness.

body.related_work: HeurtebiseEtAl2026LiMVAM, Theorem 3 and Appendix D.3, identifies the shared causal partial order and coefficients through recursive residualization under the paper's Assumption 2 correlation-and-diversity condition; it permits non-Gaussian disturbances and does not enumerate the numerical equivalence class left by partial pairing. The present result does not claim the anchor's uniqueness conclusion: it maintains component-aligned cross-view second moments and enumerates every compatible coefficient tuple from population moments. GuoPerkovic2021MinimalEffects, Theorems 2--3, motivates quotienting structural representatives by the causal output, but its recursive signatures are graphical total-effect functionals rather than covariance-dependent coefficient rows. WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration, Theorem 1, establishes AMO enumeration; Theorem 4 gives exact-once \(O(n+m)\)-delay bucket-AMO enumeration; Corollary 1 covers MPDAGs; and Theorem 5 covers PDAG consistent extensions after \(O(n^3)\) initialization. Those graph-distinct output counts can remain factorial when many orders share one numerical tuple. WangEtAl2023EquivalenceClasses, Algorithmica 85 (2023), 3003--3023, doi:10.1007/s00453-023-01131-1, gives the nearest general quotient framework, but its proof relies on local colors in a decomposable acyclic AND--OR graph; the present right congruence is instead derived from immutable numerical row projections and live-prefix pruning. DeepHuKoutris2021ProjectedEnumeration, Theorem 7, gives output-dependent delay for projected star-query enumeration after linear preprocessing, demonstrating that projection changes enumeration complexity and that output-sensitive charging can be decisive without treating causal coefficient fibers. GroneEtAl1984PositiveDefiniteCompletion supplies the completion boundary for chordal sparsity patterns; the model-specific step here uses a generating full covariance as a certificate for any arbitrary view graph on maintained inputs. AvisFukuda1996ReverseSearch provides an alternative exact enumeration paradigm but requires a locally searchable parent relation that numerical tuple classes do not supply. Bareiss1968SylvesterIdentity supplies the cited fraction-free elimination lemma underlying the proved rational output-polynomial bit-complexity result.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The main total-cost theorem is stated in an ordered exact-real model, while a separate theorem proves output-polynomial bit time and storage for rational maintained-model inputs; neither result implies floating-point stability. The algorithm gives a \(2^p\)-state-plus-output bound, not polynomial delay and not a polynomial-in-\(p\) algorithm. The q-only graph construction is valid for moment collections generated by the maintained component-aligned finite-second-moment model; an arbitrary off-model nonchordal edge array may pass every local q-test while admitting no positive-semidefinite completion. Exact enumeration over a continuum-valued covariance confidence region is not claimed. The generic write-once dynamic-programming lemma, row sorting, and integer tries are implementation machinery rather than independent causal contributions.
body.honest_scope: The contribution is confined to exact population enumeration of the coefficient-tuple frontier for a component-aligned LiMVAM subclass under an arbitrary fixed pairing graph. The generating law need not be Gaussian: each view's disturbances have centered finite-second-moment independent coordinates, while cross-view second moments are component aligned and every coordinate disturbance covariance is positive definite. These remain genuine restrictions relative to unrestricted LiMVAM, and Gaussian coordinate stacks are used only to construct existential completion witnesses. The anchor's Theorem 3 uniqueness result additionally requires its Assumption 2 correlation-and-diversity condition; the present paper does not claim that uniqueness theorem and instead enumerates all compatible tuples. The parent covariance-region inversion is reused only as the uncertainty layer after population identification; no new inferential theorem is asserted. The all-zero empty-graph reduction collapses \(p!\) orders to one tuple. Rational maintained-model inputs additionally have a proved output-polynomial bit-complexity guarantee, but floating-point stability remains outside scope.
